subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for active memory plugins, or keep file scanning, watching, and stale cleanup owned by each memory backend/plugin?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent SDK shape decides what local files third-party plugins may receive and how much of the core scanning pipeline becomes public compatibility surface.

options.title: Approve Narrow SDK Design First
options.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, batching, deletion, and test requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep Scanning Plugin-Owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may use current list/read helpers but must own watchers, indexing, deletion, and cleanup behavior themselves.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Backend Design
options.body: Defer this issue until a broader memory backend contract also decides file ingestion, search, get, writeback, and status ownership.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow SDK Design First
recommendation.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, batching, deletion, and test requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history around the memory host SDK extraction and plugin-boundary design that this decision would extend.
